templates.text: The visual system is profoundly underdeveloped, with only rudimentary light-dark discrimination possible.
Severe visual impairment results in a complete absence of fixating or tracking behaviors.
Visual processing is severely deficient, with no observable orienting response to bright stimuli.
The infant's visual channel is severely compromised, showing no blink reflex to sudden light.
Profound underdevelopment of the visual pathways prevents any meaningful processing of form or movement.
Visual input is grossly attenuated, registering only as vague, undifferentiated shadows at best.
There is a severe deficit in visual acuity, rendering the world a featureless blur.
The visual cortex shows minimal activation, resulting in a near-total lack of conscious sight.
Ocular structures are present but neural visual integration is critically impaired and non-functional.
Visual perception is absent; the eyes remain unfocused and do not converge on any target.
Severe hypoplasia of the optic nerves leads to a complete failure of visual signal transmission.
The infant demonstrates no visual awareness, with pupils that are unresponsive to light changes.
Visual development is arrested at a primitive stage, allowing only crude perception of luminance.
A profound visual deficit means the eyes do not orient toward sound or other sensory cues.
Critical underdevelopment of retinal ganglia results in no coherent visual information reaching the brain.
Visual function is severely limited to perceiving only the presence or absence of ambient light.
The visual system's severe impairment manifests as a consistent, vacant gaze with no object recognition.
Neural pathways for vision are non-functional, leaving the infant in a state of effective blindness.
There is a complete lack of visual-motor coordination, with no attempt to reach for seen objects.
Visual processing delays exceed {seconds} seconds, indicating profound central impairment.
The severe visual deficit precludes any social gaze, eye contact, or facial recognition.
Optic chiasm malformation causes a total failure of binocular visual field integration.
Visual stimuli elicit no measurable cortical response, confirming a profound sensory deprivation.
The infant's visual world is devoid of pattern, color, or defined spatial boundaries.
Agenesis of key visual association areas results in an inability to assign meaning to any sight.
Severe impairment of the visual pathway prevents the stabilization of gaze, leading to constant nystagmus.
The eyes are anatomically present but serve no functional visual purpose due to neural agenesis.
Visual perception is so deficient that even high-contrast patterns fail to elicit an attentional shift.
This severe visual channel deficit means the startle reflex is never triggered by visual threats.
The visual apparatus is critically underdeveloped, rendering the infant reliant on other senses for orientation.
